surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Wild take down the Bruins
paras: Tanner Jeannot got the scoring started for the Bruins just under two minutes in, but that’s where Boston’s luck ran out. Kirill Kaprizov tied it up for Minnesota on the power play early in the second, and Quinn Hughes put the Wild up 2-1 on the power play midway through the period. Jared Spurgeon stretched the lead to 3-1 early in the third. Kaprizov struck again into the empty net with just over a minute left.
Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Jesper Wallstedt made 26 saves for the Wild, and Michael DiPietro stopped 26 of 29.
The Bruins killed off a two-man advantage that lasted just under two minutes midway through the second. The Wild improved to 2-0-0 with a win in their home opener, and the Bruins fell to 2-1-0.
